## Overview Fixes #63565. On hybrid models with sparse retention (the default), a prefix that lives only in the CPU offload tier is never reused by a request that diverges before the single stored Mamba/sliding-window state. The offload lookup now pins a shared-prefix junction there, as the local prefix cache already does, so the prefix heals after one miss. ## Claims - A revisit that shares a prefix but diverges inside the prompt's last block hits the offload tier from the second revisit on (today: never). - No change when every group hits, when no full-attention group proves a hit, under dense retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=None`), or for models without a sliding-window/Mamba group. - A junction set by the local prefix cache is never lowered. ## Validation CPU (x86, torch 2.14.0+cpu, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k junction # main: test_sparse_group_miss_registers_shared_prefix_junction FAILED assert 0 == 16; 2 passed # this PR: 3 passed pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_offload \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py # this PR: 86 failed / 1,740 passed / 24 skipped (the same 86 fail on main) ``` The 86 failures are the same on main and are environmental on a CPU-only host: 32 in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (copies through a GPU) and 54 EC-connector cases in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` (a multimodal model config is not available there). `pre-commit run --files `: all hooks pass. GPU (4 × Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.15.4): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, TP 4, `--enforce-eager --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, 576-token blocks, GPU KV cache capped at 66K tokens (`--kv-cache-memory`) so that filler requests evict the documents from the GPU prefix cache. Serial requests. Six ~16.1K-token documents, three whose question starts inside the block that holds the stored GDN state (in-band) and three whose question starts after it (out-of-band); each is read with question A, then revisited with question B and question C, with six 16K-token fillers before each revisit. GPU prefix-cache hits were 0 on every revisit. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | in-band, revisit B | 0/3 offload hits, TTFT 1.49 s | 0/3, TTFT 1.49 s (one more GDN state stored: 0.15 vs 0.09 GB) | | in-band, revisit C | 0/3, TTFT 1.50 s | 3/3, 15,552 of ~16,140 tokens from the offload tier, TTFT 0.30 s | | out-of-band, B and C | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3 | Same documents and questions in both runs (fixed seed). The greedy answers of the three healed in-band hits equal main's answers to the same prompts, which main computed without a hit. ## Details Under sparse retention each request keeps one sparse-group checkpoint, in the last block of its prompt. A later request that shares the prefix but diverges before that block finds its full-attention chunks in the offload tier but no Mamba state at or below them, so `_lookup_complete_chunks` returns 0 for the whole request. The local prefix cache handles the same geometry by returning a shared-prefix junction from `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` (`kv_cache_manager.py:318-326`); the recompute then retains the sparse state there. The offload lookup never set one, so once the prefix had left the GPU cache every recompute stored its state inside the differing suffix again. Change (`offloading/scheduler.py`): - `_lookup_complete_chunks` records, in `RequestOffloadState.full_attention_hit_boundary`, the boundary the full-attention groups proved before the first sliding-window/Mamba group narrowed it (not on a deferred lookup). - `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, when the final hit is shorter than that boundary and retention is sparse, raises `request.shared_prefix_boundary` to it. No core change is needed: the scheduler sets the local junction before it calls the connector (`sched/scheduler.py:1077-1089`), and everything downstream reads the request field: the align split stops a chunk there (`sched/scheduler.py:610`), `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` retains it (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:511-518`), and the aligned-boundary hand-off stores it to the offload tier. Limits: the first revisit still misses (a first-visit hit needs a state retained below the replay boundary, which is the subject of #57613). Connectors that set `hit_diverged` and load nothing re-read the local junction (`sched/scheduler.py:1162-1172`) and can overwrite this one; the plain `OffloadingConnector` does not take that path. If #62278 (junction as a tuple of positions) merges first, this needs a small rebase to add the junction to `shared_prefix_boundaries`. Why this is not a duplicate: searched on 2026-10-24 for "shared_prefix_boundary", "junction", "offload shared_prefix_boundary", "offloading mamba junction" and "OffloadingConnector hybrid". #45238 is the GPU-cache form of this geometry (main has the GPU junction, #47782 / #37898); #57613 retains a block below sliding-window replay boundaries (first visit, different mechanism); #59146 keeps the prompt-end checkpoint; #56795 is a different offload-store bug; #52774 backfills GPU-local divergent hits only; #62400 adds junctions to the MooncakeStore connector; #63221 changes the connector load boundary under EAGLE. None sets a junction from the `OffloadingConnector` lookup. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write the change and the tests, and draft this text. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. ---

@@ -593,6 +593,79 @@ def test_max_load_tokens_caps_tokens_beyond_gpu_prefix():
     assert scheduler._req_status["req"].partial_tail_boundary == 24
 
 
+def _hybrid_lookup(stored: set[OffloadKey]):
+    """Full attention (group 0) holds every chunk; Mamba (group 1) only
+    the boundary states in ``stored``."""
+
+    def lookup(key: OffloadKey, req_context: ReqContext) -> LookupResult:
+        if get_offload_group_idx(key) == 0:
+            return LookupResult.HIT
+        return LookupResult.HIT if key in stored else LookupResult.MISS
+
+    return lookup
+
+
+def _make_sparse_retention_scheduler() -> OffloadingConnectorScheduler:
+    # prefix_cache_retention_interval=0, the engine default: one Mamba state
+    # per replay boundary.
+    scheduler = _make_partial_tail_scheduler()
+    scheduler.config = scheduler.config._replace(retention_interval=0)
+    return scheduler
+
+
+def test_sparse_group_miss_registers_shared_prefix_junction():
+    """A revisit that diverges before the only stored Mamba state heals.
+
+    The first request stored one Mamba state at the end of its prompt.
+    The revisit shares the first chunk (16 tokens) but not that state,
+    so the whole lookup misses. The connector must pin a junction at 16
+    so the recompute retains and offloads the Mamba state there; the next
+    revisit then hits the shared prefix.
+    """
+    scheduler = _make_sparse_retention_scheduler()
+    request = _make_partial_tail_request(scheduler)
+    request.shared_prefix_boundary = 0
+    stored: set[OffloadKey] = set()
+    scheduler.manager.lookup.side_effect = _hybrid_lookup(stored)
+
+    assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (0, False)
+    assert request.shared_prefix_boundary == 16
+
+    # The recompute's Mamba state at the junction is handed off and stored.
+    scheduler.manager.prepare_store.side_effect = lambda keys, req_context: (
+        generate_store_output(keys)
+    )
+    jobs = scheduler._build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs({"req": [(1, 77, 16)]})
+    [job_id] = jobs
+    stored.update(scheduler._jobs[job_id].keys)
+
+    scheduler._req_status["req"].transfer_jobs.clear()
+    tokens, _ = scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0)
+    assert tokens == 16
+
+
+def test_shared_prefix_junction_is_not_lowered():
+    scheduler = _make_sparse_retention_scheduler()
+    request = _make_partial_tail_request(scheduler)
+    # e.g. a longer junction from the local prefix cache
+    request.shared_prefix_boundary = 24
+    scheduler.manager.lookup.side_effect = _hybrid_lookup(set())
+
+    assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (0, False)
+    assert request.shared_prefix_boundary == 24
+
+
+def test_no_shared_prefix_junction_when_sparse_group_hits():
+    scheduler = _make_sparse_retention_scheduler()
+    request = _make_partial_tail_request(scheduler)
+    request.shared_prefix_boundary = 0
+    scheduler.manager.lookup.return_value = LookupResult.HIT
+
+    tokens, _ = scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0)
+    assert tokens == 28
+    assert request.shared_prefix_boundary == 0
+
+
 def test_max_load_tokens_rounds_down_without_partial_tail():
     scheduler = _make_partial_tail_scheduler()
     scheduler.config = scheduler.config._replace(supports_partial_tail=False)

+    def _maybe_register_shared_prefix_junction(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, boundary: int, num_hit_tokens: int
+    ) -> None:
+        """Pin a shared-prefix junction where a sparse group cut the hit, as
+        ``get_computed_blocks`` does for a local hit, so the recompute retains
+        the sliding-window/Mamba state at the full-attention hit boundary."""
+        if self.config.retention_interval is None:
+            return

+            return
+        request = req_status.req

+        if boundary > request.shared_prefix_boundary:
